citations.authors: Lichtenstein DA, Mezière GA
citations.title: Relevance of lung ultrasound in the diagnosis of acute respiratory failure: the BLUE protocol
citations.what_it_says: The bedside BLUE protocol diagnosed the cause of acute respiratory failure with ~90.5% accuracy, establishing the standardized sonographic signs used across acute-care lung US.

citations.authors: Bouhemad B, Mongodi S, Via G, Rouquette I
citations.title: Ultrasound for 'lung monitoring' of ventilated patients
citations.what_it_says: Describes the lung ultrasound score (LUS) and its use to monitor aeration changes in ventilated patients, including response to recruitment and physiotherapy.

citations.authors: Chavez MA, Shams N, Ellington LE, et al.
citations.title: Lung ultrasound for the diagnosis of pneumonia in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Pooled lung ultrasound sensitivity ~0.94 and specificity ~0.96 for pneumonia, outperforming chest radiography for bedside detection of consolidation.

citations.authors: DiNino E, Gartman EJ, Sethi JM, McCool FD
citations.title: Diaphragm ultrasound as a predictor of successful extubation from mechanical ventilation
citations.what_it_says: A diaphragm thickening fraction ≥30% predicted extubation success with 88% sensitivity and 71% specificity, validating bedside diaphragm US as a weaning-readiness tool.

citations.authors: Goligher EC, Laghi F, Detsky ME, et al.
citations.title: Evolution of diaphragm thickness during mechanical ventilation: impact of inspiratory effort
citations.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
citations.what_it_says: Diaphragm thickness fell >10% in ~44% of ventilated patients within days, driven by low inspiratory effort; establishing serial diaphragm US for monitoring ventilator-induced changes.

citations.authors: Goligher EC, Dres M, Fan E, et al.
citations.title: Mechanical ventilation-induced diaphragm atrophy strongly impacts clinical outcomes
citations.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
citations.what_it_says: Ultrasound-detected diaphragm atrophy during ventilation was associated with prolonged ventilation and complications, directly relevant to PT/RT diaphragm-protective and weaning strategies.

citations.authors: Dres M, Goligher EC, Heunks LMA, Brochard LJ
citations.title: Critical illness-associated diaphragm weakness
citations.what_it_says: Reviews the high prevalence of diaphragm weakness in critically ill patients and its link to difficult weaning, framing the clinical need for diaphragm US.

citations.authors: Lichtenstein DA
citations.title: Lung ultrasound in the critically ill
citations.what_it_says: Comprehensive review of lung US signs and protocols in the ICU, detailing how sonographic patterns differentiate interstitial syndrome, consolidation, effusion, and pneumothorax.

citations.authors: Hansell L, Milross M, Delaney A, Tian DH, Ntoumenopoulos G
citations.title: Interrater reliability in assigning a lung ultrasound score
citations.what_it_says: Demonstrated substantial interrater reliability among assessors assigning the lung ultrasound aeration score in ventilated ICU patients, supporting reproducible scoring by trained therapists.

citations.authors: Hansell L, Milross M, Delaney A, Koo CM, Tian DH, Ntoumenopoulos G
citations.title: Quantification of changes in lung aeration associated with physiotherapy using lung ultrasound in mechanically ventilated patients: a prospective cohort study
citations.what_it_says: Lung ultrasound detected measurable changes in lung aeration associated with respiratory physiotherapy in ventilated ICU patients, supporting LUS as an outcome measure for PT interventions.

citations.authors: Lockstone J, Love A, Lau YH, Hansell L, Ntoumenopoulos G
citations.title: The use of diaphragm and lung ultrasound in acute respiratory physiotherapy practice and the impact on clinical decision-making: a systematic review and meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Synthesizes evidence that diaphragm and lung ultrasound influence respiratory physiotherapists' decision-making and can evaluate treatment effects, while noting the evidence base is still developing.

citations.authors: Lau YH, Hayward S, Ntoumenopoulos G
citations.title: An international survey exploring the adoption and utility of diagnostic lung ultrasound by physiotherapists and respiratory therapists in intensive care
citations.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
citations.what_it_says: Survey of 320 ICU therapists across 30 countries found ~30% use lung US clinically; key barriers were training access, mentorship, and governance; defining the credential/training gap.

citations.authors: Smith M, Hayward S, Innes S
citations.title: A proposed framework for point of care lung ultrasound by respiratory physiotherapists: scope of practice, education and governance
citations.what_it_says: Proposes a scope-of-practice, education, and governance framework enabling respiratory physiotherapists to safely perform point-of-care lung ultrasound; the most direct PT scope anchor for this credential.

citations.authors: Ntoumenopoulos G, Pizimolas GA, Mani S, Hayward S, Lockstone J
citations.title: Lung point of care ultrasound (POCUS) in cardiorespiratory physiotherapy and respiratory therapy practices: current status and future directions
citations.what_it_says: Outlines the current state and future directions of lung POCUS within cardiorespiratory physiotherapy and respiratory therapy, including training, governance, and integration needs.
